Armattoe | | --- | | [![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Dr_Raphael_Armattoe.jpg/250px-Dr_Raphael_Armattoe.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dr_Raphael_Armattoe.jpg) | | Born | 12 August 1913 [Keta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keta "Keta"), Gold Coast | | Died | 22 December 1953(1953-12-22) (aged 40) [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg"), [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany") | | Known for | Abochi drug against parasites, 'Cure' for Swollen-Shoot | **Raphael Ernest Grail Armattoe** (12 August 1913 – 22 December 1953) was a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") scientist and political activist.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-1) He was nominated for the 1948 [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") and was a campaigner for unification of [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Togoland "British Togoland") and [French Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Togoland "French Togoland"). He was called by the _[New York Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Post "New York Post")_ "the 'Irishman' from West Africa", and the BBC producer [Henry Swanzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Swanzy "Henry Swanzy") referred to him as the "African [Paracelsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paracelsus "Paracelsus")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-2) ## Biography ### Early life and education Armattoe was born at [Keta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keta "Keta") in the [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast_(British_colony) "Gold Coast (British colony)") (in what is now the [Volta Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volta_Region "Volta Region") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")). He received his early education in [Lomé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lom%C3%A9 "Lomé"), Togoland before completing his primary education in [Denu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denu "Denu"), Gold Coast. Between 1925 and 1928 he attended secondary school at [Mfantsipim School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mfantsipim_School "Mfantsipim School"), [Cape Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Coast "Cape Coast").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) As [Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Togoland "Togoland") changed from German to British and French hands, Armattoe ended up being fluent in German, French and English; whilst also being fluent in Spanish and Portuguese.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) He also spoke his native [Ewe language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewe_language "Ewe language"). He left for [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") in 1930 for further studies, with most of his tertiary education was in Germany and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"). He apparently left Germany for France due to rising [Nazism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazism "Nazism"). He continued his studies in anthropology, literature and medicine at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) ### Research, science and medicine Armattoe moved to [Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh "Edinburgh"), where he qualified to practice medicine. He then got a locum job in [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast"), [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), and following that worked at the Civil Defence first-aid post in Brooke Park, [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), between 1939 and 1945. After the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), he opened a medical practice at his home on Northland Road in Derry.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) He later established and became the director of the Lomeshie Research Centre, named after his mother. In 1947, he attended the Nobel Prize laureation ceremonies with his friend [Erwin Schrödinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwin_Schr%C3%B6dinger "Erwin Schrödinger"), who won the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") in 1933, being the only African amongst the thousand intellectuals invited to attend the event in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) Schrödinger later wrote the foreword for Armattoe's book _The Golden Age of West African Civilization_. Armattoe later successfully applied for an anthropological research grant worth £3,000 at the time from the [Wenner-Gren Foundation for Anthropological Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenner-Gren_Foundation_for_Anthropological_Research "Wenner-Gren Foundation for Anthropological Research").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-5) The Abochi drug which can cure guinea-worms, toothaches, bronchitis, boils and allied diseases patent was later bought by a prominent Nigerian drug company at the time.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) In 1948, at the age of just 35, he was nominated for the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") by members of the [parliament of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oireachtas "Oireachtas"). The nomination was also supported by three [MPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") from [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-6) At this stage, he started being more involved with writing and giving talks, especially relating to [anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology "Anthropology"). He was described by some who knew him as a marvellous doctor and a good speaker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-fraser-7) Through association with international scientific societies he is regarded as one of the very few scientists at the time to understand atomic energy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) Later in 1948 he returned to West Africa, where he conducted research mainly on Ewe physical anthropology but also set up a medical clinic at [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi") in the [Ashanti Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashanti_Region "Ashanti Region"). He also turned his attention to poetry, writing and politics. His first collection of poems was _Between the Forest and the Sea_ (1950). His next collection, _Deep Down in the Black Man's Mind_, was published in 1954, after his death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) ### Politics Armattoe and [Kwame Nkrumah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah "Kwame Nkrumah") first met at the 1945 [Pan-African Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-African_Congress "Pan-African Congress") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester");[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-8) a conference attended by many future Ghanaians politicians as well as [Hastings Banda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings_Banda "Hastings Banda"), [Jomo Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta "Jomo Kenyatta") and [W. E. B. Du Bois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._E._B._Du_Bois "W. E. B. Du Bois").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-9) Though they both favoured independence for the colonies, Nkrumah was centrist while Armattoe was federalist. He joined the [Ghana Congress Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Congress_Party "Ghana Congress Party") rather than Nkrumah's [Convention People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_People's_Party "Convention People's Party").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) Armattoe maintained contact with Du Bois who partook in his study _Testament to Youth_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-12) He belonged to the [Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewe_people "Ewe people") ethnic group, who he sought the unification of its people who were divided by colonial powers between [British Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Togoland "British Togoland"), the Gold Coast and [French Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Togoland "French Togoland"); he wanted its people united as one Ewe nation-state being active within the [Togoland Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Togoland_Congress "Togoland Congress"), advocating for [Ewe Unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewe_Unification_Movement "Ewe Unification Movement").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-fraser-7) In 1953, Armattoe addressed the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") regarding Togoland and the "Eweland Question", which _[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Welt "Die Welt")_ at the time regarded as one of the most important documents in African history in the 20th century.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-13) ## Family His father Glikpo Armattoe was a merchant of Palime, Togoland, who traded mainly with the Germans and also studied local indigenous languages.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-14)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) Armattoe was married to Swiss-born Leony Elizabeth Schwartz, who was also known as "Marina". They had two daughters, the elder, Irusia, being born in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"). Armattoe and his family lived at Kumasi in Ghana until his death.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-15) ## Death and legacy Armattoe fell ill and died in a hospital in [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg"). His wife reported that he said he had been poisoned by some unknown persons. He had apparently been attacked previously by supporters of Kwame Nkrumah,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-fraser-7) for withholding the cure to swollen shoot unless the government approached him in a respectful manner, having chosen to distance himself from Nkrumah's Government.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-16) Inscribed on his gravestone in Hamburg are the words "Africa's Greatest Nationalist".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) A [blue plaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_plaque "Blue plaque") in his honour was unveiled by the Ulster History Circle at 7 Northland Road, Derry, where Armattoe lived from 1939 to 1945 and carried on his practice as a GP.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-18) ## Publications * _Articles, mainly on medical subjects, reprinted from periodicals_. **Raphael Ernest Grail Armattoe** (12 August 1913 – 22 December 1953) was a [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") scientist and political activist.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-1) He was nominated for the 1948 [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") and was a campaigner for unification of [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Togoland "British Togoland") and [French Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Togoland "French Togoland"). He was called by the _[New York Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Post "New York Post")_ "the 'Irishman' from West Africa", and the BBC producer [Henry Swanzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Swanzy "Henry Swanzy") referred to him as the "African [Paracelsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paracelsus "Paracelsus")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-2)

## Biography

### Early life and education

Armattoe was born at [Keta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keta "Keta") in the [Gold Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast_(British_colony) "Gold Coast (British colony)") (in what is now the [Volta Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volta_Region "Volta Region") of [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")). He received his early education in [Lomé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lom%C3%A9 "Lomé"), Togoland before completing his primary education in [Denu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denu "Denu"), Gold Coast. Between 1925 and 1928 he attended secondary school at [Mfantsipim School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mfantsipim_School "Mfantsipim School"), [Cape Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Coast "Cape Coast").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)

As [Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Togoland "Togoland") changed from German to British and French hands, Armattoe ended up being fluent in German, French and English; whilst also being fluent in Spanish and Portuguese.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) He also spoke his native [Ewe language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewe_language "Ewe language"). He left for [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") in 1930 for further studies, with most of his tertiary education was in Germany and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France").

He apparently left Germany for France due to rising [Nazism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazism "Nazism"). He continued his studies in anthropology, literature and medicine at the [Sorbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)

### Research, science and medicine

Armattoe moved to [Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh "Edinburgh"), where he qualified to practice medicine.

He then got a locum job in [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast"), [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), and following that worked at the Civil Defence first-aid post in Brooke Park, [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), between 1939 and 1945. After the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), he opened a medical practice at his home on Northland Road in Derry.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) He later established and became the director of the Lomeshie Research Centre, named after his mother.

In 1947, he attended the Nobel Prize laureation ceremonies with his friend [Erwin Schrödinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwin_Schr%C3%B6dinger "Erwin Schrödinger"), who won the [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") in 1933, being the only African amongst the thousand intellectuals invited to attend the event in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) Schrödinger later wrote the foreword for Armattoe's book _The Golden Age of West African Civilization_. Armattoe later successfully applied for an anthropological research grant worth £3,000 at the time from the [Wenner-Gren Foundation for Anthropological Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenner-Gren_Foundation_for_Anthropological_Research "Wenner-Gren Foundation for Anthropological Research").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-5) The Abochi drug which can cure guinea-worms, toothaches, bronchitis, boils and allied diseases patent was later bought by a prominent Nigerian drug company at the time.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3) In 1948, at the age of just 35, he was nominated for the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") by members of the [parliament of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oireachtas "Oireachtas"). The nomination was also supported by three [MPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament "Member of Parliament") from [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-6)

At this stage, he started being more involved with writing and giving talks, especially relating to [anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology "Anthropology"). He was described by some who knew him as a marvellous doctor and a good speaker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-fraser-7) Through association with international scientific societies he is regarded as one of the very few scientists at the time to understand atomic energy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)

Later in 1948 he returned to West Africa, where he conducted research mainly on Ewe physical anthropology but also set up a medical clinic at [Kumasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumasi "Kumasi") in the [Ashanti Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashanti_Region "Ashanti Region"). He also turned his attention to poetry, writing and politics. His first collection of poems was _Between the Forest and the Sea_ (1950). His next collection, _Deep Down in the Black Man's Mind_, was published in 1954, after his death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)

### Politics

Armattoe and [Kwame Nkrumah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah "Kwame Nkrumah") first met at the 1945 [Pan-African Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-African_Congress "Pan-African Congress") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester");[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-8) a conference attended by many future Ghanaians politicians as well as [Hastings Banda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings_Banda "Hastings Banda"), [Jomo Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta "Jomo Kenyatta") and [W. E. B. Du Bois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._E._B._Du_Bois "W. E. B. Du Bois").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-9) Though they both favoured independence for the colonies, Nkrumah was centrist while Armattoe was federalist. He joined the [Ghana Congress Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Congress_Party "Ghana Congress Party") rather than Nkrumah's [Convention People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_People's_Party "Convention People's Party").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)

Armattoe maintained contact with Du Bois who partook in his study _Testament to Youth_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-12)

He belonged to the [Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewe_people "Ewe people") ethnic group, who he sought the unification of its people who were divided by colonial powers between [British Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Togoland "British Togoland"), the Gold Coast and [French Togoland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Togoland "French Togoland"); he wanted its people united as one Ewe nation-state being active within the [Togoland Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Togoland_Congress "Togoland Congress"), advocating for [Ewe Unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewe_Unification_Movement "Ewe Unification Movement").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-fraser-7)

In 1953, Armattoe addressed the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") regarding Togoland and the "Eweland Question", which _[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Welt "Die Welt")_ at the time regarded as one of the most important documents in African history in the 20th century.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-13)

## Family

His father Glikpo Armattoe was a merchant of Palime, Togoland, who traded mainly with the Germans and also studied local indigenous languages.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-14)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4) Armattoe was married to Swiss-born Leony Elizabeth Schwartz, who was also known as "Marina". They had two daughters, the elder, Irusia, being born in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"). Armattoe and his family lived at Kumasi in Ghana until his death.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-15)

## Death and legacy

Armattoe fell ill and died in a hospital in [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg"). His wife reported that he said he had been poisoned by some unknown persons. He had apparently been attacked previously by supporters of Kwame Nkrumah,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-history-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-fraser-7) for withholding the cure to swollen shoot unless the government approached him in a respectful manner, having chosen to distance himself from Nkrumah's Government.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-16)

Inscribed on his gravestone in Hamburg are the words "Africa's Greatest Nationalist".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-3)

A [blue plaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_plaque "Blue plaque") in his honour was unveiled by the Ulster History Circle at 7 Northland Road, Derry, where Armattoe lived from 1939 to 1945 and carried on his practice as a GP.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raphael_Armattoe&printable=yes#cite_note-18)

The prizes were first awarded in 1901, marking the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-:0-2) The original Nobel Prizes covered five fields: [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry"), [physiology or medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine"), [literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), and [peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize"), specified in Nobel's will. A sixth prize, the [Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences"), was established in 1968 by [Sveriges Riksbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Riksbank "Sveriges Riksbank") (Sweden's central bank) in memory of Alfred Nobel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-:0-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-6) The Nobel Prizes are widely regarded as the most prestigious awards available in their respective fields.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Shalev8-8) Except in extraordinary circumstances, such as war, all six prizes are given annually. Each recipient, known as a [laureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureate "Laureate"), receives a [green gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrum "Electrum")[medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_medal "Nobel Prize medal") plated with [24 karat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_karat "24 karat") gold, a [diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma "Diploma"), and a monetary award. As of 2023, the Nobel Prize monetary award is 11,000,000 [kr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"), equivalent to approximately US$1,035,000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-PrizeAmount-3) No more than three individuals may share a prize, although the Nobel Peace Prize can be awarded to organisations of more than three people.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-9) Nobel Prizes are not [awarded posthumously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posthumous_award "Posthumous award"), but if a person is awarded a prize and dies before receiving it, the prize is presented.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-cbc1003-10) Between 1901 and 2026, the five Nobel Prizes and the [Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") (since 1969) were awarded 633 times to 1,018 people and organisations.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-11) Five individuals and two organisations have received more than one Nobel Prize.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-12) ## History [![Image 7: A black and white photo of a bearded man in his fifties sitting in a chair.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/AlfredNobel_adjusted.jpg/250px-AlfredNobel_adjusted.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AlfredNobel_adjusted.jpg) One story says that Alfred Nobel had the unpleasant surprise of reading his own obituary, which was titled "The Merchant of Death Is Dead", in a French newspaper Alfred Nobel was born on 21 October 1833 in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm"), Sweden, into a family of engineers.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz5-13) He was a [chemist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemist "Chemist"), [engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineer "Engineer"), and [inventor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inventor "Inventor"). In 1894, Nobel purchased the [Bofors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bofors "Bofors") iron and steel mill, which he made into a major [armaments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weapon "Weapon")[manufacturer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manufacturing "Manufacturing"). Nobel also invented [ballistite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistite "Ballistite"). This invention was a precursor to many smokeless military explosives, especially the British smokeless powder [cordite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordite "Cordite"). As a consequence of his patent claims, Nobel was eventually involved in a [patent infringement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patent_infringement "Patent infringement")[lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawsuit "Lawsuit") over cordite. Nobel amassed a fortune during his lifetime, with most of his wealth coming from his 355 inventions, of which [dynamite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamite "Dynamite") is the most famous.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz11-14) There is a popular story about how, in 1888, Nobel was astonished to read his own [obituary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obituary "Obituary"), titled "The Merchant of Death Is Dead", in a French newspaper. It was Alfred's brother [Ludvig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludvig_Nobel "Ludvig Nobel") who had died; the [obituary was eight years premature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_premature_obituaries "List of premature obituaries"). The article disconcerted Nobel and made him apprehensive about how he would be remembered. This would have inspired him to change his [will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_and_testament "Will and testament").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Time-15) Historians have been unable to verify this story and some dismiss the story as a myth.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Smiths-17) On 10 December 1896, Alfred Nobel died in [his villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Nobel "Villa Nobel") in [San Remo, Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo "Sanremo"), from a [cerebral haemorrhage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_hemorrhage "Cerebral hemorrhage"). He was 63 years old.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Sohlman13-18) Nobel wrote several wills during his lifetime. He composed the last over a year before he died, signing it at the Swedish–Norwegian Club in Paris on 27 November 1895.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Sohlman7-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-20) To widespread astonishment, Nobel's last will specified that his fortune be used to create a series of prizes for those who confer the "greatest benefit on mankind" in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics "Physics"), [chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry "Chemistry"), [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology "Physiology") or [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine "Medicine"), [literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literature "Literature"), and [peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace "Peace").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-thelocal1-21) Nobel bequeathed 94% of his total assets, 31 million SEK (c. US$186 million, €150 million in 2008), to establish the five Nobel Prizes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams7-22)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-NobelFoundationPrizeAmount-23) Owing to skepticism surrounding the will, it was not approved by the [Storting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storting "Storting") in [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway") until 26 April 1897.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz13-25-24) The [executors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executors "Executors") of the will, [Ragnar Sohlman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragnar_Sohlman "Ragnar Sohlman") and Rudolf Lilljequist, formed the [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") to take care of the fortune and to organise the awarding of prizes.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams7-8-25) Nobel's instructions named a [Norwegian Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Committee "Norwegian Nobel Committee") to award the [Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize"), the members of which were appointed shortly after the will was approved in April 1897. Soon thereafter, the other prize-awarding organisations were designated. These were the [Karolinska Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karolinska_Institute "Karolinska Institute") on 7 June, the Swedish Academy on 9 June, and the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") on 11 June.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Crawford1-26) The Nobel Foundation reached an agreement on guidelines for how the prizes should be awarded; and, in 1900, the Nobel Foundation's newly created [statutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute "Statute") were promulgated by [King Oscar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_II_of_Sweden "Oscar II of Sweden").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-thelocal1-21) ### Nobel Foundation #### Formation of Nobel Foundation Main article: [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") [![Image 8: A paper with stylish handwriting on it with the title "Testament"](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Alfred_Nobels_will-November_25th%2C_1895.jpg/250px-Alfred_Nobels_will-November_25th%2C_1895.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alfred_Nobels_will-November_25th,_1895.jpg) Alfred Nobel's [will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_and_testament "Will and testament"), which stated that 94% of his total assets should be used to establish the Nobel Prizes According to his will and testament read in Stockholm on 30 December 1896, a foundation established by Alfred Nobel would reward those who serve humanity. The Nobel Prize was funded by Alfred Nobel's personal fortune. According to the official sources, Alfred Nobel bequeathed most of his fortune to the Nobel Foundation that now forms the economic base of the Nobel Prize.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-27) The [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") was founded as a private organisation on 29 June 1900. Its function is to manage the finances and administration of the Nobel Prizes.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz14-28) In accordance with Nobel's [will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_and_testament "Will and testament"), the primary task of the foundation is to manage the fortune left to posterity by Nobel. [Robert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Nobel "Robert Nobel") and [Ludvig Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludvig_Nobel "Ludvig Nobel") were involved in the [oil business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_business "Oil business") in [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan "Azerbaijan"), and according to Swedish [historian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historian "Historian") E. Bargengren, who accessed the [Nobel family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_family "Nobel family")[archive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archive "Archive"), it was this "decision to allow withdrawal of Alfred's money from [Baku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baku "Baku") that became the decisive factor that enabled the Nobel Prizes to be established".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-29) Another important task of the Nobel Foundation is to market the prizes internationally and to oversee informal administration related to the prizes. The foundation is not involved in the process of selecting the [Nobel laureates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_laureates "Nobel laureates").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz15-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman16-31) In many ways, the Nobel Foundation is similar to an [investment company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment_company "Investment company"), in that it invests Nobel's money to create a solid funding base for the prizes and the administrative activities. The Nobel Foundation is [exempt from all taxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_exemption "Tax exemption") in Sweden (since 1946) and from investment taxes in the United States (since 1953).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz17-18-32) Since the 1980s, the foundation's investments have become more profitable and as of 31 December 2007, the assets controlled by the Nobel Foundation amounted to 3.628 billion Swedish _kronor_ (c. US $560 million).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz15-17-33) According to the statutes, the foundation consists of a board of five Swedish or Norwegian citizens, with its seat in Stockholm. The [chairman of the board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_board "Chairman of the board") is appointed by the Swedish [King in Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privy_Council_of_Sweden "Privy Council of Sweden"), with the other four members appointed by the [trustees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trustee "Trustee") of the prize-awarding institutions. An [executive director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_director "Executive director") is chosen from among the [board members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_directors "Board of directors"), a deputy director is appointed by the King in Council, and two deputies are appointed by the [trustees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trustees "Trustees"). However, since 1995, all the members of the board have been chosen by the trustees, and the executive director and the deputy director appointed by the board itself. As well as the board, the Nobel Foundation is made up of the prize-awarding institutions (the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institute, the Swedish Academy, and the [Norwegian Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Committee "Norwegian Nobel Committee")), the trustees of these institutions, and [auditors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audit "Audit").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz15-17-33) #### Foundation capital and cost The capital of the Nobel Foundation today is invested 50% in [shares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Share_capital "Share capital"), 20% [bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_(finance) "Bond (finance)") and 30% other [investments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investments "Investments") (e.g. [hedge funds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_funds "Hedge funds") or [real estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_estate "Real estate")). The distribution can vary by 10 percent.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-dn20121202-34) At the beginning of 2008, 64% of the funds were invested mainly in American and European stocks, 20% in bonds, plus 12% in real estate and hedge funds.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-handelsblatt2008-35) In 2011, the total annual cost was approximately 120 million [kronor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"), with 50 million kronor as the prize money. Further costs to pay institutions and persons engaged in giving the prizes were 27.4 million kronor. The events during the Nobel week in Stockholm and Oslo cost 20.2 million kronor. The administration, Nobel [symposium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_conference "Academic conference"), and similar items had costs of 22.4 million kronor. The cost of the [Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_Sciences "Economic Sciences") prize of 16.5 Million kronor is paid by the [Sveriges Riksbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Riksbank "Sveriges Riksbank").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-dn20121202-34) ### Inaugural Nobel prizes [![Image 9: A black and white photo of a bearded man in his fifties sitting in a chair.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/R%C3%B6ntgen%2C_Wilhelm_Conrad_%281845-1923%29.jpg/250px-R%C3%B6ntgen%2C_Wilhelm_Conrad_%281845-1923%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:R%C3%B6ntgen,_Wilhelm_Conrad_(1845-1923).jpg) [Wilhelm Röntgen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_R%C3%B6ntgen "Wilhelm Röntgen"), who received the first [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") for his discovery of the [X-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-ray "X-ray") Once the Nobel Foundation and its guidelines were in place, the [Nobel Committees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Committee "Nobel Committee") began collecting nominations for the inaugural prizes. Subsequently, they sent a list of preliminary candidates to the prize-awarding institutions. The Nobel Committee's Physics Prize shortlist cited [Wilhelm Röntgen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_R%C3%B6ntgen "Wilhelm Röntgen")'s discovery of [X-rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-ray "X-ray") and [Philipp Lenard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philipp_Lenard "Philipp Lenard")'s work on [cathode rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathode_ray "Cathode ray"). The Academy of Sciences selected Röntgen for the prize.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman134-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Leroy117-118-37) In the last decades of the 19th century, many chemists had made significant contributions. Thus, with the Chemistry Prize, the academy "was chiefly faced with merely deciding the order in which these scientists should be awarded the prize".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz77-38) The academy received 20 nominations, eleven of them for [Jacobus van 't Hoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobus_Henricus_van_'t_Hoff "Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Crawford118-39) Van 't Hoff was awarded the prize for his contributions in [chemical thermodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_thermodynamics "Chemical thermodynamics").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz81-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman205-41) The Swedish Academy chose the poet [Sully Prudhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sully_Prudhomme "Sully Prudhomme") for the first Nobel Prize in Literature. A group including 42 Swedish writers, artists, and literary critics protested against this decision, having expected [Leo Tolstoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_Tolstoy "Leo Tolstoy") to be awarded.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz144-42) Some, including [Burton Feldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burton_Feldman "Burton Feldman"), have criticised this prize because they consider Prudhomme a mediocre poet. Feldman's explanation is that most of the academy members preferred [Victorian literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_literature "Victorian literature") and thus selected a Victorian poet.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman69-43) The first Physiology or Medicine Prize went to the German physiologist and microbiologist [Emil von Behring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_von_Behring "Emil von Behring"). During the 1890s, von Behring developed an [antitoxin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antitoxin "Antitoxin") to treat [diphtheria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diphtheria "Diphtheria"), which until then had been causing thousands of deaths each year.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman242-244-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Leroy233-45) The first [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") went to the Swiss [Jean Henri Dunant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Dunant "Henry Dunant") for his role in founding the International [Red Cross Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Red_Cross_and_Red_Crescent_Movement "International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement") and initiating the Geneva Convention, and jointly given to French pacifist [Frédéric Passy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Passy "Frédéric Passy"), founder of the Peace League and active with Dunant in the Alliance for Order and Civilization. ### Second World War In 1938 and 1939, [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler")'s [Third Reich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") forbade three laureates from Germany ([Richard Kuhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Kuhn "Richard Kuhn"), [Adolf Friedrich Johann Butenandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Butenandt "Adolf Butenandt"), and [Gerhard Domagk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Domagk "Gerhard Domagk")) from accepting their prizes.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz23-46) They were all later able to receive the diploma and medal.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Wilhelm85-47) Even though Sweden was officially neutral during the Second World War, the prizes were awarded irregularly. In 1939, the Peace Prize was not awarded. No prize was awarded in any category from 1940 to 1942, due to the [occupation of Norway by Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_occupation_of_Norway "German occupation of Norway"). In the subsequent year, all prizes were awarded except those for literature and peace.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-48) During the occupation of Norway, three members of the Norwegian Nobel Committee fled into exile. The remaining members escaped persecution from the Germans when the Nobel Foundation stated that the committee building in [Oslo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo "Oslo") was Swedish property. Thus it was a safe haven from the German military, which was not at war with Sweden.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams23-49) These members kept the work of the committee going, but did not award any prizes. In 1944, the Nobel Foundation, together with the three members in exile, made sure that nominations were submitted for the Peace Prize and that the prize could be awarded once again.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz23-46) ### Prize in Economic Sciences Main article: [Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") [![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Worldmapnobellaureatesbycountry2.PNG/250px-Worldmapnobellaureatesbycountry2.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Worldmapnobellaureatesbycountry2.PNG) Map of Nobel laureates by country After [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics") evolved rapidly as an academic discipline and came to be increasingly recognized as a significant scientific field.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-50) In 1968, Sweden's central bank, [Sveriges Riksbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Riksbank "Sveriges Riksbank"), celebrated its 300th anniversary and donated a sum of money to the [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") to be used to set up a new award in the field of [economic sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_sciences "Economic sciences"). The following year, 1969, the [Prize in Economic Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") was awarded for the first time. [The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") is required to select the economics laureate in the same way as it does for the science Nobel Prizes. The first laureates for the Economics Prize were [Jan Tinbergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Tinbergen "Jan Tinbergen") and [Ragnar Frisch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragnar_Frisch "Ragnar Frisch"), "for having developed and applied dynamic models for the analysis of economic processes".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman343-51)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz207-52) The board of the Nobel Foundation decided that after this addition, it would allow no further new prizes.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz20-53) ## Award process The award process is similar for all of the Nobel Prizes, the main difference being who can make nominations for each of them.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman16-17-54) [Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/75/Announcement_Nobelprize_Chemistry_2009-3.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original) The 2009 announcement of the laureates in [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry") by [Gunnar Öquist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnar_%C3%96quist "Gunnar Öquist"), permanent secretary of the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") [Video 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/be/Announcement_Nobelprize_Literature_2009-1.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original) The 2009 [Nobel Prize in Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature") announcement by [Peter Englund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Englund "Peter Englund") in Swedish, English, and German ### Nominations Nomination forms are sent by the Nobel Committee to about 3,000 individuals, usually in September the year before the prizes are awarded. These individuals are generally prominent academics working in a relevant area. Regarding the Peace Prize, inquiries are also sent to governments, former Peace Prize laureates, and current or former members of the Norwegian Nobel Committee. The deadline for the return of the nomination forms is 31 January of the year of the award.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman16-17-54)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz26-55) The Nobel Committee nominates about 300 potential laureates from these forms and additional names.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams15-56) The nominees are not publicly named, nor are they told that they are being considered for the prize. All nomination records for a prize are sealed for 50 years from the awarding of the prize.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman315-57)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-58) Main article: [List of Nobel laureates §50-year secrecy rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#50-year_secrecy_rule "List of Nobel laureates") ### Selection The Nobel Committee then prepares a report reflecting the advice of experts in the relevant fields. This, along with the list of preliminary candidates, is submitted to the prize-awarding institutions.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman52-59) There are four awarding institutions for the six prizes awarded: * [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") – Chemistry; Physics; Economics * [Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Assembly_at_the_Karolinska_Institute "Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute") – Physiology / Medicine * [Swedish Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Academy "Swedish Academy") – Literature * [Norwegian Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Committee "Norwegian Nobel Committee") – Peace The institutions meet to choose the laureate or laureates in each field by a majority vote. Their decision, which cannot be appealed, is announced immediately after the vote.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz25-28-60) A maximum of three laureates and two different works may be selected per award. Except for the Peace Prize, which can be awarded to institutions, the awards can only be given to individuals.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams8-61) The winners are announced by the awarding institutions during the first two weeks of October. ### Posthumous nominations Although posthumous nominations are not presently permitted, individuals who died in the months between their nomination and the decision of the prize committee were originally eligible to receive the prize.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-62) This has occurred twice: the 1931 Literature Prize awarded to [Erik Axel Karlfeldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Axel_Karlfeldt "Erik Axel Karlfeldt"), and the 1961 Peace Prize awarded to [UN Secretary General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations")[Dag Hammarskjöld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld "Dag Hammarskjöld"). Since 1974, laureates must be thought alive at the time of the October announcement. There has been one laureate, [William Vickrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Vickrey "William Vickrey"), who in 1996 died after the prize (in [Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences")) was announced but before it could be presented.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams9-63) On 3 October 2011, the laureates for the [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") were announced; however, the committee was not aware that one of the laureates, [Ralph M. Steinman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_M._Steinman "Ralph M. Steinman"), had died three days earlier. The committee reconsidered Steinman's award, since the rule is that the prize is not awarded posthumously,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-cbc1003-10) but decided that as the decision to award Steinman the prize "was made in good faith", it would remain unchanged, and the prize would be awarded.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-64) ### Recognition time lag Nobel's will provided for prizes to be awarded in recognition of discoveries made "during the preceding year". Early on, the awards usually recognised recent discoveries.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-65) However, some of those early discoveries were later discredited. For example, [Johannes Fibiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Fibiger "Johannes Fibiger") was awarded the 1926 Prize in [Physiology or Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine") for his purported discovery of a parasite that caused cancer.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz125-66) To avoid repeating this embarrassment, the awards increasingly recognised scientific discoveries that had withstood the test of time.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams25-67)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-embo-68)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-scienceline1-69) According to Ralf Pettersson, former chairman of the Nobel Prize Committee for Physiology or Medicine, "the criterion 'the previous year' is interpreted by the Nobel Assembly as the year when the full impact of the discovery has become evident."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-embo-68) [![Image 11: A room with pictures on the walls. In the middle of the room there is a wooden table with chairs around it.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Nobelinstituttet_20080913-01.jpg/250px-Nobelinstituttet_20080913-01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nobelinstituttet_20080913-01.jpg) The committee room of the Norwegian Nobel Committee The interval between the award and the accomplishment it recognises varies from discipline to discipline. The Literature Prize is typically awarded to recognise a cumulative lifetime body of work rather than a single achievement.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-70)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-71) The Peace Prize can also be awarded for a lifetime body of work. For example, 2008 laureate [Martti Ahtisaari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martti_Ahtisaari "Martti Ahtisaari") was awarded for his work to resolve international conflicts.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-73) However, they can also be awarded for specific recent events.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-74) For instance, [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan") was awarded the 2001 Peace Prize just four years after becoming the Secretary-General of the United Nations.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams330-75) Similarly [Yasser Arafat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasser_Arafat "Yasser Arafat"), [Yitzhak Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin "Yitzhak Rabin"), and [Shimon Peres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimon_Peres "Shimon Peres") received the 1994 award, about a year after they successfully concluded the [Oslo Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords "Oslo Accords").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams27-76) A [controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_controversies "Nobel Prize controversies") was caused by awarding the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize to [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") during his first year as US president.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-77)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-78) Awards for physics, chemistry, and medicine are typically awarded once the achievement has been widely accepted. Sometimes, this takes decades – for example, [Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subrahmanyan_Chandrasekhar "Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar") shared the 1983 Physics Prize for his 1930s work on stellar structure and evolution.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-currentscience-79)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-80) Not all scientists live long enough for their work to be recognised. Some discoveries can never be considered for a prize if their impact is realised after the discoverers have died.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-82)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-83) ## Award ceremonies and related events [![Image 12: Two men standing on a stage. The man to the left is clapping his hands and looking towards the other man. The second man is smiling and showing two items to an audience not seen on the image. The items are a diploma which includes a painting and a box containing a gold medal. Behind them is a blue pillar clad in flowers.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Horbjorn_Jagland_presents_President_Barack_Obama_with_the_Nobel_Prize_medal_and_diploma.jpg/120px-Horbjorn_Jagland_presents_President_Barack_Obama_with_the_Nobel_Prize_medal_and_diploma.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Horbjorn_Jagland_presents_President_Barack_Obama_with_the_Nobel_Prize_medal_and_diploma.jpg) [![Image 13: A man in his fifties standing behind a desk with computers on it. On the desk is a sign reading "Kungl. Vetensk. Akad. Sigil".](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Giovanni_Jona-Lasinio-Nobel_Lecture-2.jpg/250px-Giovanni_Jona-Lasinio-Nobel_Lecture-2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Giovanni_Jona-Lasinio-Nobel_Lecture-2.jpg) Right: [Giovanni Jona-Lasinio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Jona-Lasinio "Giovanni Jona-Lasinio") presenting [Yoichiro Nambu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoichiro_Nambu "Yoichiro Nambu")'s Nobel Lecture at [Aula Magna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aula_Magna_(Stockholm_University) "Aula Magna (Stockholm University)") in Stockholm in 2008; Left: [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") after receiving the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo City Hall from Norwegian Nobel Committee chairman [Thorbjørn Jagland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorbj%C3%B8rn_Jagland "Thorbjørn Jagland") in 2009 Except for the Peace Prize, the Nobel Prizes are presented in Stockholm, Sweden, at the annual Prize Award Ceremony on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death. The recipients' lectures are normally held in the days prior to the award ceremony. The Peace Prize and its recipients' lectures are presented at the annual Prize Award Ceremony in Oslo, Norway, usually on 10 December. The award ceremonies and the associated banquets are typically major international events.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-autogenerated5-84)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-thelocal2-85) The Prizes awarded in Sweden's ceremonies are held at the [Stockholm Concert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_Concert_Hall "Stockholm Concert Hall"), with the Nobel banquet following immediately at [Stockholm City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_City_Hall "Stockholm City Hall"). The Nobel Peace Prize ceremony has been held at the [Norwegian Nobel Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Institute "Norwegian Nobel Institute") (1905–1946), at the [auditorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auditorium "Auditorium") of the [University of Oslo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oslo "University of Oslo") (1947–1989), and at [Oslo City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_City_Hall "Oslo City Hall") (1990–present).[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Levinovitz21-23-86) The highlight of the Nobel Prize Award Ceremony in Stockholm occurs when each Nobel laureate steps forward to receive the prize from the hands of the [King of Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Sweden "Monarchy of Sweden"). In Oslo, the chairman of the Norwegian Nobel Committee presents the Nobel Peace Prize in the presence of the [King of Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Norway "Monarchy of Norway") and the [Norwegian royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_royal_family "Norwegian royal family").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-thelocal2-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-sweden2-87) At first, King [Oscar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_II_of_Sweden "Oscar II of Sweden") did not approve of awarding grand prizes to foreigners.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-88) ### Nobel Banquet Main article: [Nobel Banquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Banquet "Nobel Banquet") [![Image 14: A set table with a white table cloth. There are many plates and glasses plus a menu visible on the table.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Nobel-banquet-table.jpg/250px-Nobel-banquet-table.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nobel-banquet-table.jpg) Table at the 2005 [Nobel Banquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Banquet "Nobel Banquet") in Stockholm After the award ceremony in Sweden, a banquet is held in the [Blue Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Hall "Blue Hall") at the [Stockholm City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_City_Hall "Stockholm City Hall"), which is attended by the [Swedish Royal Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Royal_Family "Swedish Royal Family") and around 1,300 guests. The [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") banquet is held in Norway at the [Oslo Grand Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Hotel_(Oslo) "Grand Hotel (Oslo)") after the award ceremony. Apart from the laureate, guests include the president of the [Storting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storting "Storting"), on occasion the Swedish prime minister, and, since 2006, the King and Queen of Norway. In total, about 250 guests attend. ### Nobel lecture According to the statutes of the Nobel Foundation, each laureate is required to give a public lecture on a subject related to the topic of their prize.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-89) The Nobel lecture as a rhetorical genre took decades to reach its current format.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-90) These lectures normally occur during Nobel Week (the week leading up to the award ceremony and banquet, which begins with the laureates arriving in Stockholm and normally ends with the Nobel banquet), but this is not mandatory. The laureate is only obliged to give the lecture within six months of receiving the prize, but some have happened even later. For example, US President [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt") received the Peace Prize in 1906 but gave his lecture in 1910, after his term in office.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams18-19-91) The lectures are organised by the same association which selected the laureates.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-92) > Military cemeteries in every corner of the world are silent testimony to the failure of national leaders to sanctify human life. —[Yitzhak Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin "Yitzhak Rabin"), 1994 Nobel Peace Prize lecture[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-93) ### Nobel Minds From 1959 to 1990, Swedish journalist [Bengt Feldreich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengt_Feldreich "Bengt Feldreich") gathered the science prize laureates to a discussion, broadcast as _Snillen spekulerar_ (in English _Science and Man_) first in radio, and then from the mid-1960s in [Sveriges Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Television "Sveriges Television"). Since 2004, the program is a coproduction with [BBC World News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_World_News "BBC World News") under the title _Nobel Minds_, since 2011 hosted by [Zeinab Badawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeinab_Badawi "Zeinab Badawi").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-94)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-95) ## Prizes ### Medals Main article: [Nobel Prize medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_medal "Nobel Prize medal") [![Image 15: A heavily decorated paper with the name "Fritz Haber" on it.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Nobel_Prize_Diploma_Fritz_Haber_1918.JPG/250px-Nobel_Prize_Diploma_Fritz_Haber_1918.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nobel_Prize_Diploma_Fritz_Haber_1918.JPG) [Fritz Haber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritz_Haber "Fritz Haber")'s diploma is shown, which he received for the development of a method to synthesise [ammonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ammonia "Ammonia"). Laureates receive a heavily decorated diploma together with a gold medal and prize money The Nobel Foundation announced on 30 May 2012 that it had awarded the contract for the production of the five (Swedish) Nobel Prize medals to Svenska Medalj AB. Between 1902 and 2010, the Nobel Prize medals were minted by [Myntverket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myntverket "Myntverket") (the Swedish Mint), which ceased operations in 2011 after 107 years. In 2011, the Mint of Norway, located in Kongsberg, made the medals. The Nobel Prize medals are registered trademarks of the Nobel Foundation.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-96) Each medal features an image of Alfred Nobel in left profile on the [obverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obverse_and_reverse "Obverse and reverse"). The medals for physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, and literature have identical obverses, showing the image of Alfred Nobel and the years of his birth and death. Nobel's portrait also appears on the obverse of the Peace Prize medal and the medal for the Economics Prize, but with a slightly different design. For instance, the laureate's name is engraved on the rim of the Economics medal.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman2-97) The image on the reverse of a medal varies according to the institution awarding the prize. The reverse sides of the medals for chemistry and physics share the same design.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Paulingmedal-98) All medals made before 1980 were struck in 23 [carat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carat_(purity) "Carat (purity)") gold. Since then, they have been struck in 18 carat [green gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloured_gold#Green_gold "Coloured gold") plated with 24 carat gold. The weight of each medal varies with the value of gold, but averages about 175 grams (0.386 lb) for each medal. The diameter is 66 millimetres (2.6 in) and the thickness varies between 5.2 millimetres (0.20 in) and 2.4 millimetres (0.094 in).[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-99) Because of the high value of their gold content and tendency to be on public display, Nobel medals are subject to medal theft.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-UniversityofCalifornia-100)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-NYTimes-101)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Reuters-102) During World War II, the medals of German scientists [Max von Laue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_von_Laue "Max von Laue") and [James Franck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Franck "James Franck") were sent to Copenhagen for safekeeping. When Germany invaded Denmark, Hungarian chemist (and Nobel laureate himself) [George de Hevesy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_de_Hevesy "George de Hevesy") dissolved them in [aqua regia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqua_regia "Aqua regia") (nitro-hydrochloric acid), to prevent confiscation by [Nazi Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") and to prevent legal problems for the holders. After the war, the gold was recovered from solution, and the medals re-cast.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman397-103) ### Diplomas [![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Nobel_Prize_diplom_Wilhelm_Conrad_R%C3%B6ntgen.jpg/250px-Nobel_Prize_diplom_Wilhelm_Conrad_R%C3%B6ntgen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nobel_Prize_diplom_Wilhelm_Conrad_R%C3%B6ntgen.jpg) The Nobel diploma awarded to [Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_Conrad_R%C3%B6ntgen "Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen") in 1901 Nobel laureates receive a diploma directly from the hands of the King of Sweden, or in the case of the peace prize, the chairman of the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Each diploma is uniquely designed by the prize-awarding institutions for the laureates that receive them.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman2-97) The diploma contains a picture and text in Swedish which states the name of the laureate and normally a citation of why they received the prize. None of the Nobel Peace Prize laureates has ever had a citation on their diplomas.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams18-104)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-105) ### Award money [![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Nobel_Prize_-_Prize_money_%281901-2023%29.svg/250px-Nobel_Prize_-_Prize_money_%281901-2023%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nobel_Prize_-_Prize_money_(1901-2023).svg) Evolution of the prize amount between 1901 and 2023, adjusted for inflation The laureates are given a sum of money when they receive their prizes, in the form of a document confirming the amount awarded.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Feldman2-97) The amount of prize money depends upon how much money the Nobel Foundation can award each year. The purse has increased since the 1980s, when the prize money was 880,000 SEK per prize (c. 2.6 million SEK altogether, US$350,000 today). In 2009, the monetary award was 10 million SEK (US$1.4 million).[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Nobel_Prize_Amounts-106)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-CNN-107) In June 2012, it was lowered to 8 million SEK.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-108) If two laureates share the prize in a category, the award grant is divided equally between the recipients. If there are three, the awarding committee has the option of dividing the grant equally, or awarding one-half to one recipient and one-quarter to each of the others.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-Abrams8-10-109)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-110)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-111) It is common for recipients to donate prize money to benefit scientific, cultural, or humanitarian causes.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-112)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-113) As of 2026, the monetary award per prize category is 12 million Swedish kronor (SEK), equivalent to approximately US$1.221 million.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize#cite_note-PrizeMoney-114) ## Statistics * **Youngest person to receive a Nobel Prize:**[Malala Yousafzai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malala_Yousafzai "Malala Yousafzai"); at the age of 17, received [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") (2014). * **Oldest person to receive a Nobel Prize:**[John B.
